title: Partial-label Learning with Mixed Closed-set and Open-set Out-of-candidate Examples

problem.claim: Partial-label learning must handle training examples whose true labels may lie outside their assigned candidate label sets.

gap.claim: Existing PLL assumptions do not accommodate out-of-candidate examples, including both closed-set and open-set cases.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces PLL with out-of-candidate examples and distinguishes closed-set and open-set types.
The method uses candidate and non-candidate label losses with criteria to dynamically differentiate OOC examples.
It applies reversed label disambiguation to closed-set OOC examples and dynamically assigned random candidate-label regularization to open-set OOC examples.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art PLL methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: PLL assumes that each training example's true label belongs to its candidate label set.
Real-world data may violate this assumption, producing examples whose true labels are outside the assigned candidate sets.
The paper defines OOC examples and separates them into closed-set and open-set types.
The approach differentiates OOC types and uses type-specific disambiguation or regularization during training.
The authors report that the method outperforms state-of-the-art PLL methods in extensive experiments.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, evaluation metrics, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide the detailed criteria, loss formulation, regularization parameters, or computational requirements.
